definitions.gloss: plain form; plain style; informal style
definitions.explanation: The grammatical style of Japanese that uses dictionary forms of verbs and adjectives without the polite です/ます endings. Used in casual conversation, internal monologue, writing, and as the base form for many grammatical constructions.

examples.japanese: ⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{普通体|ふつうたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: I speak in plain form with friends.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{教科書|きょうかしょ}→教科書：01085_kyoukasho⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{普通体|ふつうたい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{丁寧体|ていねいたい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{違|ちが}い→違い：03432_chigai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}びます→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: In this textbook, you learn the difference between plain form and polite form.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日記|にっき}→日記：01486_nikki⟧や⟦{小説|しょうせつ}→小説：01434_shousetsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{普通体|ふつうたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}かれる→書く：00477_kaku⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Diaries and novels are often written in plain style.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{普通|ふつう}→普通：01502_futsuu⟧ (ordinary, normal) and ⟦{体|たい}→体：09872_tai⟧ (style, form). A key grammatical term used in Japanese language education to describe the informal style of speech and writing.

The {普通体|ふつうたい} is not inherently rude — it is simply the unmarked, neutral form of Japanese. It is required in many grammatical contexts even within polite speech, such as before ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧, {時|とき}, and many other subordinate clause patterns. Mastering when to use {普通体|ふつうたい} versus {丁寧体|ていねいたい} is one of the central challenges for learners.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {普通体|ふつうたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧: to speak in plain form
- {普通体|ふつうたい}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧: to write in plain form
- {普通体|ふつうたい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{変|か}える→変える：01089_kaeru⟧: to change to plain form
- {普通体|ふつうたい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{丁寧体|ていねいたい}: plain form and polite form

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {常体|じょうたい}: plain style — a more formal linguistic term for the same concept, often used in Japanese grammar textbooks written in Japanese
- {丁寧体|ていねいたい}: polite style — the contrasting style that uses です/ます endings
- {敬体|けいたい}: polite style — synonym of {丁寧体|ていねいたい}, used in more technical linguistic discussions
- {辞書形|じしょけい}: dictionary form — the base form of a verb specifically, whereas {普通体|ふつうたい} refers to the overall style
